frank: Noticed a p99 latency spike on the int8 perf canary this morning after the rolling deploy :grimacing:
frank: p50 stable, but p99 up ~120ms vs yesterday on the same model/seq len distribution
leah: ugh. which release/merge did we roll?
frank: rolled canary of main @ 1941200000 (includes PR#3534) around 02:10 UTC
omar: PR3534 is the 'deconv batch matcher + kernel scheduler tweak' right?
frank: yep. that touched kernel selection heuristics and added an early layout conversion for quant path
ben: can you paste the bench output?
frank: pasted below from perf-bench-canary (same test harness):
frank: ```
frank: tokens/sec: baseline (yesterday) 1850
frank: tokens/sec: canary (now)      1510  # ~18% drop
frank: p99 latency: baseline 220ms -> canary 340ms
frank: CPU% host-side handler up 12%
frank: perf counters show extra memcpy calls on dequant path
frank: ```
leah: extra memcpy screams layout conversion in hot path. do we have a flamegraph?
frank: uploading flame: https://internal-perf/fg/194123 (highlights memcpy and dequant shim)
omar: looked at the flame: kernel selector picks "deconv_alt" kernel for int8 when batch size==1 now. old policy chose "deconv_v1" which avoids a transpose.
ben: so the new kernel has better avg throughput but higher fixed setup cost (layout convert) => harms p99 small-batch requests
frank: exactly. our canary traffic is ~60% small interactive (<8 tokens) which amplifies the setup cost
leah: can we short-circuit to the old kernel for small batch or for quantized models?
omar: quick patch idea: in selector.py change rule order: prefer kernels that are layout-preserving if seq_len<32 or batch==1 for quantized dtypes
ben: does CI have microbench that would catch this? I saw a failing perf CI on the nightly job which flagged PR3534 earlier but it was borderline and got ignored because avg improved
ci-bot: Perf CI summary for PR3534: avg throughput +6%, p99 latency +38ms (regression), threshold flagged but not blocking due to config
frank: that matches. we need a canary rollback or a targeted selector tweak. rollback will be fastest to restore SLA
leah: for immediate mitigation: revert PR3534 on canary, then push a focused selector fix to main behind a flag. Can someone bisect to confirm PR3534 is the root?
omar: did a quick git bisect locally across recent merges -> pointed to PR3534 as first bad commit. verified by running small-batch microbench locally (script: `tools/perf/run_small_batch.sh`)
ben: ok confirm. I'll open a revert PR to canary now. then we can iterate on selector heuristics in a follow-up.
frank: filing ticket with repro instructions, perf logs, and suggested selector change:
frank: ```
frank: repro: run `tools/perf/interactive_bench --model gpt-small --dtype int8 --seq 16 --batch 1 --duration 60`
frank: artifacts: flamegraph link, perf counters (memcpy counts), canary bench outputs
frank: suggested change: in kernel_selector.match(), prefer kernels where `preserves_layout=True` when `dtype in (int8,int4)` and `(batch==1 or seq_len<32)`
frank: ```
leah: also add a CI microbench regression test targeting p99 for small-batch int8 path so we don't ignore p99 delta next time :+1:
ben: revert PR created: #3579 (revert PR3534) and rolling back canary now :robot_face:
ci-bot: deploy status: canary rollback started -> nodes draining -> expected completion 02:46 UTC
omar: I'll work on a branch `fix/selector-quant-small-batch` with the heuristic and a perf test. will run on staging before re-landing
frank: thanks. let's also audit other kernel rules that prioritized throughput over setup cost (fp8? int4?)
leah: good call. leaving follow-up task for wider audit: INFRA-1202
ben: tl;dr: revert applied to canary, bisect points to PR3534, follow-up selector heuristic + CI microbench to prevent regression. :white_check_mark:
frank: thanks team :heart:
